fatal_errors: The proposed Ti/Hf alloying intervention does not reconstruct the demonstrated Re addition.

The mechanism omits the observed Re-induced grain refinement, lattice distortion, excess free volume, amorphous grain-boundary regions, and their role as defect sinks suppressing helium-bubble segregation.
The claimed preservation of performance up to 1600 °C is unsupported; the target evidence concerns room-temperature irradiation and mechanical testing of sputtered films.
No prior evidence is cited for Ti/Hf improving both ductility and helium-irradiation tolerance while retaining a single BCC phase.
The falsification criterion is qualitative and does not separately test phase stability, bubble size and distribution, irradiation hardening, or grain-boundary embrittlement.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the broad objective and uses untreated NbMoTaW as the baseline, but it proposes a materially different and unevidenced intervention. The target study added equiatomic Re to nanocrystalline sputtered NbMoTaW films and tested 120 keV He implantation at room temperature to 1 × 10^16 ions/cm². Its key evidence was suppression of grain-boundary helium bubbles, hardening, and embrittlement through Re-induced grain refinement and defect-sink-rich distorted or amorphous boundary structures. The generated hypothesis instead invokes generic enhanced diffusion from Ti/Hf, provides no evidence, and extrapolates to 1600 °C. Its experiment could provide preliminary comparison data but lacks quantitative thresholds and the microscopy and mechanical measurements needed to discriminate the proposed mechanism.
